origin.description: Create a survival object from a timeline style data set. This will almost always be the response variable in a formula.
origin.details: When used in a coxph or survfit model, Surv2 acts as a trigger to internally convert a timeline style data set into counting process style data. The repeated argument controls how repeated instances of the same event code are treated.
origin.value: An object of class Surv2. There are methods for print, is.na and subscripting.

translation.description: Create a survival object from a timeline style data set. This will almost always be the response variable in a formula.
translation.details: When used in a coxph or survfit model, Surv2 acts as a trigger to internally convert a timeline style data set into counting process style data. The repeated argument controls how repeated instances of the same event code are treated.
translation.value: A Surv2 timeline response with time and status columns.
translation.example:
from survival.surv2 import FactorEvent, Surv2

a = Surv2([1, 2.5, 10, float("nan")], [1, 0, 1, 1])
b = Surv2(
    [70, 72, 75, 78],
    FactorEvent(["CU", "CU", "MCI", "dementia"], ["CU", "MCI", "dementia"]),
)
print(" ".join(a.character()))
print(" ".join(b.character()))
